newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Indian tariff cuts seen boosting Australian wool.
newsitem.headline: Indian tariff cuts seen boosting Australian wool.

text.p: The Indian government's recent ratification of significant cuts to import duties on apparel wool has opened the way for increased Australian wool sales and better access to the Indian domestic clothing market, the Federal Department of Primary Industries and Energy (DPIE) said.

DPIE was commenting on India's cut in tariffs on imports of raw apparel wool (greasy, scoured and carbonised) to 20 percent from 25 percent and on wool tops to 40 percent from 50 percent. A temporary additional surcharge of two percent applies to the products, giving effective rates of 22 percent and 42 percent respectively.

The Indian government's decision to cut wool tariffs across the board in 1997/98 indicated the country would become increasingly important to the future wellbeing of the Australian wool industry, DPIE's international wool section director David Navin said in the department's Primary Resource newsletter.
"India is an important emerging market for Australian wool and for the first nine months of 1996/97 exports increased by 26 percent," he said.

"India's strong tradition of wool use and growing middle class domestic consumption are expected to continue to increase. Its competitive manufacturing sector also provides a strong base for the export market," he said.
The improved access follows discussions which began in 1996 between Australia and Indian officials.
Australia has offered to assist the Indian industry over the next few years in developing its wool textiles and wool production industries.
